properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory for an Ethereum smart-contract contest submission (2020, ChrisWhinfrey). hash.js@1.1.3 is pinned in package-lock.json (lines 395-400) as a transitive dependency of the Hardhat/ethers toolchain (via elliptic/ethereum-cryptography). The package ships SHA-1/SHA-224/256/384/512 and RIPEMD-160. No first-party JS call site found — the first-party code is Solidity; the algorithm ships in the build's dependency tree. Changeable here by pruning/upgrade in the lockfile.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory for the vendored OpenZeppelin upgradeable contracts tree used by submission11 (2022, DanielVonFange). crypto-js@3.3.0 pinned in lib/openzeppelin-contracts-upgradeable/package-lock.json (lines 6051-6053) as a transitive dependency of the OZ JS tooling. crypto-js ships SHA-1, MD5, SHA-2, AES, DES, PBKDF2, HMAC; SHA-1 is its flagship digest. No first-party call site found. Changeable here by pruning the lockfile.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory spanning the three Hardhat/foundry toolchain lockfiles of submissions 15 (2020) and 11 (2022): the secp256k1 npm package (^4.0.1, native secp256k1 ECDSA/ECDH bindings) plus @types/secp256k1, pulled in transitively by ethers/ethereumjs/hardhat for Ethereum key and transaction signing. Quantum-relevant (Shor breaks ECDSA on secp256k1). No first-party JS call site found — first-party code is Solidity; the toolchain ships and invokes secp256k1. Changeable here only at the toolch

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory spanning the same three toolchain lockfiles: the evp_bytestokey npm package (^1.0.0/^1.0.3), an OpenSSL EVP_BytesToKey implementation (single-round MD5 password-to-key KDF), pulled in transitively by the crypto-browserify/browserify stream shims under Hardhat/ganache. Weak KDF by modern standards (no salt/work factor), quantum-safe but CWE-relevant. No first-party call site found. Changeable here only through the toolchain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile-declared dependency: bcrypt-pbkdf (bcrypt-cross-over PBKDF used by the sshpk/ethereum Node stack) appears in the package-lock.json files of submission15 (2020) and the vendored openzeppelin-contracts[-upgradeable] trees (2022). All 15 sites are dependency-manifest entries — the dependency inventory. No application-level bcrypt call site found in the Solidity source.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile-declared dependency: create-ecdh@4.x (Node ECDH binding) is a transitive dep of the browserify/ethereumjs stack in submission15 (2020) and the vendored openzeppelin-contracts[-upgradeable] trees (2022). The build ships ECDH-capable code; no application call site found — this is the dependency inventory. Quantum relevance: ECDH is Shor-breakable, but here it exists only as toolchain capability.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory for submission15 (2020): tweetnacl@0.14.5 is resolved in package-lock.json (lines 2096-2098, declared as ^0.14.3 by an upstream package) and ships Ed25519 signing/verification. Transitive dependency of the Hardhat/ethers toolchain (sshpk/http-signature family). Quantum-relevant: Ed25519 is Shor-vulnerable. No first-party call site found — first-party code is Solidity; the algorithm ships in the build's dependency tree. Changeable here only through the toolchain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory for submission15 (2020): tweetnacl@0.14.5 (resolved at package-lock.json lines 2096-2098) also ships X25519 scalar multiplication (nacl.scalarMult) for Diffie-Hellman key agreement. Shor-vulnerable key agreement — harvest-now-decrypt-later class if ever used on captured traffic. No first-party call site found; ships in the build's dependency tree as a transitive npm dep.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory for submission15 (2020): tweetnacl@0.14.5 (resolved at package-lock.json lines 2096-2098) ships XSalsa20-Poly1305 (nacl.secretbox) authenticated encryption. This one is post-quantum-appropriate symmetric AEAD (256-bit keys, Grover only) — the rating A+ reflects that. No first-party call site found; ships in the build's dependency tree as a transitive npm dep.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider in the build: tweetnacl (0.14.5 under submission15's toolchain, ^1.0.3 entries in the OZ lockfiles) is declared across the workspace lockfiles as a transitive npm dependency. It ships Ed25519 signatures, X25519 DH, XSalsa20-Poly1305 AEAD, SHA-512, and the XSalsa20 stream cipher. Presence is what the inventory records: the toolchain installs it whether or not the Solidity-first-party code calls it, and it is reachable through any JS the build runs. Changeable here only at the tool

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider in the build: crypto-js@3.3.0 declared in the vendored openzeppelin-contracts-upgradeable lockfile (resolved at lines 6051-6053, required as ^3.1.9-1 by an upstream package). Ships a broad classical suite: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-2, HMAC, AES/DES/TripleDES (CBC/ECB), PBKDF2, RC4-drop, Rabbit. Presence is the inventory fact; reachable by any JS the toolchain runs. Changeable here by pruning/upgrading in the lockfile.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto dependency in submission15's (2020) toolchain: sha.js@2.4.11, the streaming SHA-1/SHA-224/SHA-256/384/512 implementation, declared as a transitive dependency in package-lock.json (required by hash-base/create-hash style packages under Hardhat). Presence is the inventory fact; no first-party JS call site found in the Solidity-first-party codebase. Changeable here only at the toolchain level.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto dependency in the vendored OZ-upgradeable toolchain of submission11 (2022): bcryptjs@2.4.3 (pure-JS bcrypt password hashing, resolved at package-lock.json lines 4619-4621, required as ^2.3.0 at line 10600 by an upstream test tooling package). bcrypt is a password KDF/verifier — quantum-safe (memory-hard, Grover-limited) but an inventory item with a work factor.
